subject: Transient gen-api ladder spike — triage, mitigation asks & external note
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] gen-api p95 ladder spike (us-west-2)

Heads-up — automated SLO alert triggered for gen-api (us-west-2) at 09:00 PDT: p95 token latency jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s across the last 6m window, throughput steady but tail increased.

Quick facts:
- Tenants: ~1.7k active connections at the time; top affected account (by token volume): BrightCart (approx 18% of window).
- Error rate: no spike in 5xx, but a subset of requests show repeated KV cache misses and longer kernel exec times on one pool.
- Initial trace attached (genapi_trace_usw2_20280410.jsonl) and p95_trend_plot.png.

Immediate asks: can SRE/serving runtime look at kernel scheduling and KV eviction logs for pool-g2-03? If the pool is degraded we should consider proactive routing to pool-g2-05 and start drafting an external note to BrightCart.

Ben
SRE Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: genapi_trace_usw2_20280410.jsonl (trace excerpt), p95_trend_plot.png

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api p95 ladder spike (us-west-2)

Thanks Ben — on it. Karthik / Diego: please triage kernel exec times + KV eviction pattern on pool-g2-03. Priorities:
1) Confirm whether the spike is localized to pool-g2-03 or cross-pool. If localized, aggressive reroute to pool-g2-05 (warm) for affected models.
2) If reroute is non-disruptive, start a controlled route shift for BrightCart traffic only (they're heavy in this window).
3) If reroute not possible, list fallback options (reduce batch size, force quantized variant for burst, temporary throttling).

Marissa — can you prepare a short customer note for BrightCart; we should be transparent with impact and ETA to resolution but avoid technical jargon. Draft below is a starter — please edit.

Draft customer note (Marissa: please revise):
Subject: Brief service update — transient latency increase
Hi Jordan —
We observed a transient increase in API response times affecting some BrightCart requests in the us-west region. Our engineering team is actively investigating and we expect mitigation within the next 2 hours. We’ll share a follow-up with root cause and any corrective steps. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts checkout flows and we’re prioritizing BrightCart traffic.
Best,
Aisha on behalf of Redwood Inference Ops

I'll hold on public messaging until you confirm reroute viability. Attaching the trace for context.

— Aisha
Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: customer_note_draft_brightcart_v1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api p95 ladder spike (us-west-2) — customer note suggestion

Thanks — I tweaked the customer note to be concise and customer-facing. Two clarifying asks: a quick ETA on mitigation (best guess) and whether we have a temporary mitigation we can offer BrightCart to reduce checkout latencies (e.g., rerouting their traffic or enabling a shorter context window).

Proposed note to send once you confirm mitigation plan:
Subject: Temporary latency increase affecting some API requests — update
Hi Jordan —
We want to let you know that we detected a temporary increase in response times for a subset of API requests in the us-west region earlier today. Our team has prioritized BrightCart traffic and implemented mitigations to restore normal response times. We expect ongoing stabilization over the next hour.
We’ll provide a follow-up with a short summary and any recommended configuration changes. If you’re seeing any user-facing issues right now, please share an example request ID and we’ll prioritize that trace.
Thanks for the patience — we’ll keep you updated.
Best,
Marissa 
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

I can send this to Jordan immediately once engineering confirms reroute and an ETA.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api p95 ladder spike (us-west-2) — mitigation complete

Update and quick post-mortem notes:
- Mitigation: we identified a scheduling contention on pool-g2-03 caused by a degraded kernel path on the A100 instance (driver-level regression coincident with a recent infra package). We drained ~22% of BrightCart traffic off pool-g2-03 and shifted to pool-g2-05; p95 reduced from 1.8s -> 380ms within 8 minutes of the shift.
- No request-level 5xx increase observed, no data loss.
- Next steps: roll back the infra package on g2-03 nodes and run a canary; add an automated routing rule that prefers pool-g2-05 for BrightCart until kernel fix lands; create an SRE runbook entry for detecting similar kernel scheduling regressions.

Aisha / Marissa: you can now send the customer note. Suggested brief message: publish Marissa's proposed note with a single line about mitigation and a promise of a follow-up summary and RCA within 48 hours.

Ben and Diego: please attach the completed trace and a short ops timeline to the RCA. I’ll file the incident (GENAPI-4721) and link to the HubSpot deal.

Karthik
Servings Runtime Lead
Redwood Inference
